subject: Nimble Memory Use and Changing Constants in Simulations

messages.author: cd5bd8ad5174fb68
messages.subject: Nimble Memory Use and Changing Constants in Simulations
parts:
Hello Nimble Users and Developers!

I am currently trying to run many simulations from a model, following: https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/simulation_from_model.html. I am trying to run these simulations in a for loop, and in each loop, changing the constants in the model. Doing so uses a very large amount of memory on my computer until it crashes. I was wondering if anybody had any advice for dealing with these memory use problems, or ideas for how to navigate doing this without building/compiling the model every single time (which I'm pretty sure I have to do if I'm changing constants in each loop). Or maybe a way in which to remove the build up of files like DLLs? Any thoughts would be great.

#### Example Code####
# this isn't meant to be executable, just to outline the issue/what I'm doing...
# I can send more detailed code if necessary...

nsims = 100
for (i in 1:nsims){

my.constants = list(covariate = rnorm(nyears, mean[i], sd[i]))

model = nimbleModel(code = code, constants = my.constants, inits = initial.values,
                                       calculate = F)
nodesToSim = model$getDependencies(c("params"), self = F, downstream = F)
model$simulate(nodesToSim)
} # VERY SLOW

Thanks!!!

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Nimble Memory Use and Changing Constants in Simulations
parts: TJ, thanks for your question.  If you pass the "covariate" as an initial value into your model, rather than a constant, then you can change the value of "covariate" inside the model, without rebuilding the model.  Something like:

model = nimbleModel(code = code, constants = my.constants, inits = initial.values,
                                       calculate = F)
nodesToSim = model$getDependencies(c("params"), self = F, downstream = F)

new.initial.values = list(covariate = rnorm(nyears, mean[i], sd[i]))
model$setInits(new.initial.values)
model$simulate(nodesToSim)
} # VERY SLOW

Also, it looks like you're doing the model$simulate(...) call using the uncompiled model.  It will be much faster if you use a compiled model object.  Code for that might look like:

model = nimbleModel(code = code, constants = my.constants, inits = initial.values,
                                       calculate = F)
nodesToSim = model$getDependencies(c("params"), self = F, downstream = F)

new.initial.values = list(covariate = rnorm(nyears, mean[i], sd[i]))
compiled.model$setInits(new.initial.values)
compiled.model$simulate(nodesToSim)
} # MAYBE FASTER

Let me know if this helps.

Cheers,
Daniel
